**![](data:image/png;base64,)**
A type of array-like data structure that contains the element and the reference to the next piece of data. The first node is called the "header" because it only contains a reference to the next element/piece of data. A node contains a value and a link (reference) to the next node.

## Use cases
---
Should be used in cases when constant time insertion and removal is needed, and the data structure
## Doubly Linked List
---
Like a normal linked list, but the reference to both the preceding and succeeding node are stored.
Node structure:
```
class Node {
	Object data;
	Node next;
	Node previous;
}
```
This type of linked list makes it easier to find elements, but it requires more maintenance when inserting and deleting elements. It also requires more storage.
**![516](data:image/png;base64,)**
## Methods
---
Since a linked list implements a collection, we need to implement `.add` and `.remove`.

```
public T remove(T target) {
	Node curr = header;
	Node prev = null;
	while (curr != null) {
		if (curr.data.compareTo(target) == 0) {
			if (header == curr) {
				header = curr.next;
			} else {
				prev.next = curr.next;
				// You have removed the target node
			}
			return target;
		}
		prev = curr;
		curr = curr.next;
	}
	return null;
}
```

---
Good scenarios to test:
+ When list is empty or has one elem
+ Processing take place at beginning or end of the list (like for insertion)
